finding.claim: The app takes the caller's identity from the client-supplied request header X-Session-User-Verified. Nothing in this code authenticates the request or checks that a trusted proxy set the header. Any client can send the header with another user's name and pass the ACL checks as that user. This is an authentication bypass and horizontal privilege escalation. It is exploitable only if no fronting proxy strips or overwrites the header. That proxy is outside this repo, so it could not be checked.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled HTTP header X-Session-User-Verified on any request
finding.sink: delete_file (del STORE[fid]) and rename_file (f['name'] = ...) via ensure_allowed/is_allowed, which trust g.user

trace.note: g.user = request.headers.get('X-Session-User-Verified') with no signature, session or proxy-origin validation
is_allowed checks the claimed user name against resource grants, so an impersonated owner name passes

finding.guards_checked: Looked for session or token verification, an HMAC or signature on the header, and a check of the request source. None exists in this repo. The ACL in acl.py is only as strong as g.user. No authentication decorator and no header-stripping middleware are present. Any proxy that overwrites the header is not in this repo. A missing header gives g.user=None, which matches no grant, so only a forged header is a bypass.

verdict.guard_found: none in repo. The ACL checks (acl.py:9-10 abort(403), views.py:25 tested bool) work correctly, but they only validate g.user. No signature check, session check or header-stripping middleware exists.
verdict.reason: Every traced line is accurate (views.py:11 reads the header unauthenticated, views.py:17 and :25 pass it to the ACL, acl.py:5 matches the name against grants), but whether a client can forge X-Session-User-Verified depends on a fronting proxy outside this repo, which the "Verified" header name suggests may overwrite it.

verdict_facts.guard_found: Trusted upstream identity middleware per maintainer facts, which supplies X-Session-User-Verified. In the code, ensure_allowed (acl.py:9-10) aborts 403 and is_allowed (views.py:25) is tested. Nothing in this directory validates the header itself.
verdict_facts.reason: The trace is accurate (views.py:11, 17, 25; acl.py:5), but the maintainer states request identity such as g.user is populated by trusted upstream middleware, so the "Verified" header at views.py:11 is treated as trusted and the spoofing premise, which the candidate admits depends on a proxy it could not check, is excluded.
